Heard the counsel for the parties.

The present petition has been filed challenging the order dated 13.4.2010 passed by the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), District Agra under Sections 30/31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as Act, 1894).

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), District Agra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts of the case are that the petitioner was admittedly the original tenure holder of Plot No.168 (Area 2.4210 Hectare) situated at Village Pali Sadar, Pargana and Teshil Kirawali, Police Station Kirawali, District Agra.

sentences.text: The case of respondent no.6 is that the petitioner executed an agreement to sale on 18.7.2005 in favour of respondent no.6 regarding the aforesaid plot and earnest money of Rs.2,00,000/- was also paid to the petitioner under the said agreement to sale.

However, when no sale deed was executed by the petitioner, the respondent no.6 instituted Original Suit No.130 of 2006 for specific performance of contract before the Civil Judge (Senior Division), District Agra.
The said suit was instituted on 6.2.2006.

Subsequently, a notification under Section 4 of the Act, 1894 was issued by the State Government on 14.8.2008 and subsequently, a notification under Section 6 of the Act,
1894 acquiring the disputed plot was issued by the Court on 27.5.2009.

A final award of Rs.1,09,07,200/- regarding the disputed plot was declared on 12.4.2010 by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Agra and as the petitioner was the recorded tenure holder of the said plot, the award was declared in favour of the petitioner.

However, the respondent no.6 claimed compensation for the disputed plot on the basis of agreement to sale and therefore, filed an application before the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Agra on 11.3.2010 for the said purpose.

The Additional District Magistrate(Land Acquisition), Agra vide his impugned order dated 13.4.2010 held that as the petitioner was the recorded tenure holder of the disputed plot, therefore, compensation was to be paid to the petitioner but as a dispute between the parties was pending before the Civil Court,
therefore, recommendation was made by the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition),
Agra that the amount be deposited in the Court under Section 31 of the Act, 1894.
The said order dated 13.4.2010 has been challenged in the present petition.
During the pendency of the writ petition, the parties entered into a compromise wherein the petitioner admitted the payment of Rs.2,00,000/- as earnest money in pursuance to the agreement to sale.
Under the compromise, the parties have agreed that the respondent no. 6 be paid 1/3rd of the compensation amount and the petitioner be paid 2/3rd of the compensation amount.

The said compromise was filed in Original Suit No.130 of 2006 and after the said compromise was verified,
Original Suit No.130 of 2006 has been decreed in terms of the compromise.

The compromise as well as the order dated 13.7.2019 decreeing Original Suit No.130 of 2006 has been filed along with a supplementary affidavit in the present petition and is admitted by the parties and their counsel.

In view of the compromise admitted by the parties, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition) District Agra and the District Judge, Agra that the compensation as declared under the award dated 12.4.2010 be apportioned between the petitioner and respondent no.6 in accordance with the compromise decree passed in Original Suit No.130 of 2006 and be paid to the parties as above.
With the aforesaid directions, the writ petition is disposed of.
